title: Cheapest Route
description:
A road network has n towns numbered 1 to n and m two-way roads. Each road connects two towns and has a positive travel cost. Find the minimum total cost to travel from town s to town t, or print -1 if t cannot be reached from s.

Input format
Line 1: n and m.
Next m lines: three integers u, v, w describing a road between towns u and v with cost w.
Last line: s and t.

Output format
One integer: the minimum total cost, or -1.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= m <= 200000, 1 <= w <= 1000000. There may be several roads between the same pair of towns. The answer fits in a 64-bit signed integer.
hints: Counting roads (as breadth-first search does) is not enough because roads have different costs.
Dijkstra's algorithm: keep the best known distance to each town, and repeatedly settle the unsettled town with the smallest distance, relaxing its roads.

Use a min-heap of (distance, town). When you pop a pair whose distance is larger than the recorded best, skip it. Stop early when you pop t. Distances can exceed 32 bits, so use a 64-bit type in C++ and Java.

examples.explanation: Town 3 has no roads, so it cannot be reached.
